newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo Wellcome makes push for Japanese growth.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo Wellcome makes push for Japanese growth.

text.p: Glaxo Wellcome Plc, seeking a greater share of the world's second biggest market, bought the remaining 50 percent of its Japanese joint venture Nippon Glaxo for 354 million pounds ($596 million) Thursday.

Analysts said they had long expected Glaxo to buy out Japanese partner Shin Nihon Jitsugyo Co. Ltd, which will also get a 7.7 million pounds ($1.38 billion) payout in lieu of the venture's 1996 dividend.
Nippon Glaxo develops, produces and markets prescription medicines across Japan.

After setting up a series of Japanese joint ventures since the early 1980s, Glaxo has moved to take them over in a bid to carve out a greater share in Japan's lucrative marketplace, second only to the United States in terms of profitability and sales.
